Featured · AI prompt engineering for finance & marketing

Q4 Marketing Strategy

I took one messy marketing brief and built the same Q4 strategy three ways, then compared how much risk and ambiguity each method exposed before any money is committed.

0Prompting methods compared
0Shared source brief
0Customer segments targeted
0Figures taken from the brief
1Read the brief
2Separate facts from assumptions
3Run 3 prompt methods
4Compare risks surfaced
5Final strategy

What the project is

A prompt engineering project comparing Naive, Persona and Tree-of-Thoughts prompting on the same Q4 marketing brief.

What it is based on

A messy brief: confirmed numbers mixed with assumptions, one unreliable data source and two competing lead targets. No outside figures were added.

NAIVE

Single plain prompt

Fast answer in one pass. Assumptions and the unreliable source stay buried in the text.

PERSONA

Strategist and analyst

One clear approach per segment: a 10% loyalty offer for active users and a 30% win-back offer for unengaged users.

TREE OF THOUGHTS

Experts that critique

A data analyst, strategist and finance expert challenged each other and caught contradictions and missing data.

Hidden risk surfaced before launch qualitative, relative

Naive
Low
Persona
Medium
Tree of Thoughts
Highest
Result: all three approaches agreed on the confirmed data. What differed was how much hidden risk each one surfaced, and Tree of Thoughts surfaced the most.
Prompt engineeringTree of ThoughtsAssumption auditData-quality reviewSegment-level offers

Prototype built from the supplied brief only, with no live link to ad platforms or customer databases.
